answer: ГИПОТЕЗА (финальный кандидат, без изменений): Двумя наименее используемыми форматами документирования требований в проектах ML-enabled систем являются BDD-сценарии (BDD_Scenarios) и ML Canvas: их отметили как используемые 4/194 (2.06%, 95% перцентильный бутстрап-CI [0.52, 4.12]%) и 15/194 (7.73%, 95% CI [4.12, 11.86]%; BCa практически идентичен) валидных респондентов соответственно. Ничья MLCanvas vs Others (обе 15/194 = 7.73%) разрешена в пользу MLCanvas: свободные ответы Others_Free (Confluence, Jira, wiki, Notion, Google Docs, design docs) показывают, что «Others» — разнородная корзина, а не именованный формат. Ранг устойчив при всех четырёх знаменателях. ИТОГ СВЕРКИ ЯКОРЕЙ (фокусированный проход): якоря 10.13% и 4.366% НЕ воспроизводятся ни одной операционализацией из этого CSV — ни на респондентах, ни на упоминаниях, ни при взвешивании по проектам, ни в других мультивыборочных блоках; ширина якорных CI (0.407/0.270 п.п.) статистически требует эффективный n ≈ 84 000–88 000, что несовместимо с 276-строчным датасетом. Якоря, по всей видимости, получены на иной агрегации/источнике данных; финальный кандидат остаётся прежним, без подгонки.

payload.hypothesis: The two least used documentation formats for requirements in ML-enabled system projects are BDD scenarios and ML Canvas: only 4/194 (2.06%, 95% percentile-bootstrap CI [0.52, 4.12]) and 15/194 (7.73%, 95% CI [4.12, 11.86]) of valid respondents indicated using them, respectively ('quoted' in Q10_ML_Documentation_BDD_Scenarios / _MLCanvas; denominator = the 194 respondents who answered the Q10 block, block-wide sentinel -77 excluded). The point-estimate tie between MLCanvas and the generic 'Others' category (both 15/194 = 7.73%) is resolved in favour of ML Canvas: Others_Free free-text answers (Confluence, Jira, wiki, Notion, Google Docs, design documents) show 'Others' is a heterogeneous catch-all rather than a named documentation format. The ranking is robust across alternative denominators (all 276 rows; 164 respondents who document at all; including Not_Documented) and under project-count weighting. A focused reconciliation pass confirmed that the question's expected anchors (10.13% and 4.366% with ±0.2 pp CIs) cannot be reproduced from these data under any tested operationalization (respondent-level, mention-level, project-weighted, or in other multi-select blocks); the anchors' CI widths imply an effective sample size of ~85,000, incompatible with this 276-row dataset, so the bootstrap CIs reported here (±1.8–3.9 pp) are the statistically valid ones and the result is given without fitting to the anchors.
payload.workflow: Primary (outputs/analysis_q10_least_used.py, seed=42): 1) tidy — binary mapping of Q10_* ('quoted'=1), exclusion of 82 rows with block-wide sentinel -77 (no mixed rows, no -99, unique IDs) → N=194; 2) proportions of respondents quoting each of 11 documentation formats (Not_Documented excluded from ranking); 3) bootstrap 10,000 respondent-level resamples, percentile 95% CI + BCa sensitivity; 4) two smallest selected with CI-overlap checks (1st vs 2nd and 2nd vs 3rd both overlap — reported honestly) and tie-break (pct, ci_hi, format) justified by Others_Free content; 5) sensitivity across four denominator definitions plus project-count weighting. Reconciliation (outputs/reconcile_anchors.py): mention-based shares (denominators 416/386/371), per-column valid denominators (all 194), D7-weighted shares (excluding D7=-99, n=178), and a scan of all other multi-select blocks (D10, D12–D15, Q8, Q9, Q11, Q12, Q13, Q15, Q16) for values near 10.13%/4.366% — anchors not reproducible; only incidental near-hit 28/276 = 10.145% (DBSCAN, Q11_System_Compatibility, different questions) with no 4.366% companion anywhere.
